clue.text: Arrangements for containment of dispute set back?

indicators.note: back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the containment of a phrase is the run of letters held inside it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A question about how a quarrel might be shelved by putting arrangements in place to contain it.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'Arrangements for containment' as the definition, but 'containment of' is the hidden-word signal, so the definition is just 'Arrangements'. SPUTES sits inside 'dispute set' and 'back' turns it round.
explanation.definitionFit: Organisational structures or layouts are set-ups, plural to match the plural clue word.

clue.text: Where you'll see world's attention on Thursday

indicators.note: in a down clue one piece placed on another sits above it

parts.note: to give ear is to pay attention

explanation.surface: A notice says where the world's eyes will be turned this Thursday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' puts EAR above TH in the down light; 'Where you'll see' only sets the scene.
explanation.definitionFit: Our planet, the globe we live on, is commonly called the world.

clue.text: Careless, showing a French film with lots of nude coupling

parts.note: un is the French for a

indicators.note: coupling here means the letters are joined together and mixed up
lots of a word, but not all of it, drops its final letter

explanation.surface: Someone is careless for showing a French film full of naked couples.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coupling' reads as sex in the film, but it signals letters joined and mixed; 'lots of' means most of a word, losing its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Heedless people pay no attention, the sense of the adjective careless.

clue.text: Group questioned by pollsters is small enough

parts.note: ample means plentiful, enough

explanation.surface: A complaint that the group surveyed by pollsters is barely adequate in size.
explanation.definitionFit: Opinion pollsters survey a selected subset of people meant to represent the population.

clue.text: Missing handle? That's unheard-of

explanation.surface: An object without its handle is described as something nobody has heard of.
explanation.definitionFit: Handle is slang for a name, so without one you are anonymous; obscure and unknown things are likewise anonymous, never named.

clue.text: Proud boast of happy couple, not for the likes of us?

definitions.text: Proud boast of happy couple, not for the likes of us?

parts.words: Proud boast of happy couple, not for the likes of us?
parts.note: a contented pair boast that they never quarrel, while puzzle solvers could not claim to go without the grid they love

explanation.surface: A happily married pair boast they have never argued, something the rest of us could not claim.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it is the couple's boast of no angry words; split the last two words together and it describes a life without puzzles, which the solvers ('the likes of us') would never choose.
explanation.definitionFit: Spouses who never quarrel say no angry remark ever passed between them, a stock boast of harmony.

clue.text: Stoker turned over fish to reveal veined appearance

indicators.note: turned over means the first name is read from the end back

parts.note: Bram Stoker wrote Dracula
the ling is a fish of the cod family

explanation.surface: A man feeding a furnace flips a fish and finds streaks running through it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stoker' looks like a boilerman but is the author Bram Stoker.
explanation.definitionFit: Streaked patterning like that of polished stone is called marbling.

clue.text: Grub found in cellar vault

indicators.note: found in says the letters lie inside the words that follow

explanation.surface: Something crawling turns up in an underground vault.
explanation.definitionFit: A grub is an insect in its immature, wormlike stage.

clue.text: car, in cash

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'car, in cash' (9): it is cut short, with no definition or anagram indicator; the letters of 'car in cash' give the answer but the rest of the clue is missing.

clue.text: Original agency propose putting out old-fashioned text-book

indicators.note: the schoolbook is spread out so that it holds the other word inside

parts.note: a primer is an elementary schoolbook, a term now dated
to move a motion is to propose it

explanation.surface: An agency is formed by someone proposing that a dated schoolbook be withdrawn.
explanation.walkthrough: 'putting out' means the schoolbook is extended so that it surrounds the proposal, which lands just before its final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: In philosophy the first cause of all motion, the original agent behind everything, is the prime mover.

clue.text: Nation following start of remembrance service

indicators.note: following puts the second piece after the first
the start of a word is its first letter

parts.note: an ace is an unreturnable serve in tennis

explanation.surface: A country stages a service of remembrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'service' looks religious, tied to remembrance, but it is a tennis serve.
explanation.definitionFit: A people of common descent, a nation, can be called a race.

clue.text: Thriller writer about to meet trainer

parts.note: c, for circa, means about
a handler trains and controls animals such as dogs

explanation.surface: A crime novelist is about to meet his coach.
explanation.walkthrough: Raymond Chandler wrote hard-boiled detective novels such as The Big Sleep.
explanation.definitionFit: Raymond Chandler was an American author of crime thrillers.

clue.text: Hate being poorly accommodated in a hotel

indicators.note: badly housed letters are put in the wrong places, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone detests being given a poor room in a hotel.
explanation.definitionFit: To detest something intensely is to loathe it.

clue.text: Fellow able to pull back from quarrel

indicators.note: pull back means the whole run of letters is drawn back the other way

parts.note: fit means able, capable

explanation.surface: A man is able to withdraw from a row.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiff is a petty squabble or minor disagreement.

clue.text: Diverts money produced by investment with Society

parts.note: interest is the money paid on invested capital

explanation.surface: An investor's returns are channelled through a building society.
explanation.definitionFit: To divert someone is to amuse or engage them, which is what a verb sense of interest also means.

clue.text: Belt designed for use in RUC etc

indicators.note: designed means the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A belt is made for use in the Royal Ulster Constabulary and similar forces.
explanation.walkthrough: The RUC was the Royal Ulster Constabulary, Northern Ireland's police until 2001.
explanation.definitionFit: A girdle worn round the waist is called a cincture.

clue.text: Change of direction in stratagem for dealing with Xanthippe?

indicators.note: dealing with suggests handling the letters and shuffling them
south becomes north: one compass point is swapped for the opposite one

explanation.surface: A scheme for handling Socrates' notoriously difficult wife.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Change of direction in' swaps the S (south) of STRATAGEM for N (north); 'dealing with' rearranges NTRATAGEM. Xanthippe, wife of Socrates, was famed as a shrew, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: Xanthippe is a byword for a scolding wife, and a violent, overbearing woman is a termagant: definition by example.

clue.text: Resolute person voluming of nets

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Resolute person voluming of nets' (8): 'voluming' is garbled and no source gives the printed words; the wordplay appears to reverse TRAWLS round AT but the indicators cannot be recovered.

clue.text: Weapon that's literally about to be used in a fight

indicators.note: to be used in a word is to be put inside it

parts.note: a set-to is a fight or brawl

indicators.note: about here means the abbreviation is turned round

explanation.surface: A blade that, quite literally, is about to come out in a brawl.
explanation.walkthrough: 'literally' gives its dictionary abbreviation; 'about' turns that round to TIL, and 'to be used in' places it after the first letter of a set-to, a brawl.
explanation.definitionFit: A stiletto is a slim dagger with a tapering blade.

clue.text: Mark showing initial reduction-here's a different currency

indicators.note: the opening letter is removed, so the word is reduced at its start

parts.note: a brand is a mark burned or stamped on something

explanation.surface: An old German mark is devalued at the start, giving way to another country's money.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Mark' suggests the old German currency, which is why the definition says 'a different currency'.
explanation.definitionFit: The rand is the monetary unit of South Africa.

clue.text: He sometimes fills envelopes

parts.note: He is the chemical symbol of a light gas, and the envelopes are the gasbags of balloons and airships rather than postal stationery

explanation.surface: A man is sometimes given the job of stuffing envelopes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'He' reads as a man stuffing letters; it is the chemical symbol, and 'envelopes' are balloon gasbags.
explanation.definitionFit: This light inert gas, symbol He, is used to inflate balloons and airships.

clue.text: Blair as he was in 1984?

parts.note: Blair is not the prime minister but Eric Blair, and 1984 is the novel he published under his pen name, not the year

explanation.surface: A question about what the politician Blair was like back in 1984.
explanation.walkthrough: Eric Arthur Blair wrote Nineteen Eighty-Four under a pseudonym; the surface points to Tony Blair, a new MP in 1984.
explanation.definitionFit: Eric Blair's pen name, under which he wrote Nineteen Eighty-Four, was George Orwell.

clue.text: Seeking inspiration, a lot

annotationWithheld.why: Clue held as 'Seeking inspiration, a lot' (5): no reading of these words gives the answer (perhaps ERA for 'a lot' of time plus a missing TO), so the clue looks cut short, and no source gives the rest.

clue.text: Heartlessly carries on fouling up predicted series of events

indicators.note: fouling up means the letters are messed up and rearranged
heartlessly means the central letter of the word is removed

explanation.surface: Someone keeps on making a mess of a forecast of how things will unfold.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heartlessly' drops the middle R of CARRIES, giving CARIES; with ON, 'fouling up' rearranges those letters.
explanation.definitionFit: A scenario is a postulated sequence of future developments.

clue.text: House with low doorway decapitated big John

indicators.note: a word decapitated loses its first letter

parts.note: john is slang for a lavatory, as is loo

explanation.surface: A tall man named John has his head cut off by a low door frame.
explanation.walkthrough: 'big John' looks like a man's name; 'John' is a lavatory (loo) and 'big' loses its head. An igloo's entrance is a low tunnel.
explanation.definitionFit: An Inuit snow dwelling is entered through a low tunnel, the low doorway that defines it.

clue.text: Mountain, very big, with an attractive quality

parts.note: OS stands for outsize, a clothing size
SA is short for sex appeal

explanation.surface: A huge mountain that also has a striking beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: Ossa is a mountain in Thessaly, Greece, famous from the myth of piling Pelion on Ossa.
explanation.definitionFit: Ossa is a peak in Greece, named in myths of giants piling up summits.

clue.text: Able to catch stale smell associated with tropical starling — it's awful

indicators.note: to catch something is to hold it inside

parts.note: BO is body odour, a stale smell
the mina, or myna, is an Asian starling

explanation.surface: A competent bird-catcher gets a whiff of a stale odour from a tropical starling.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Able' looks like the adjective that starts the sentence, but it is the container; the smell and the bird go in after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dreadful or appalling is abominable.

clue.text: Operational research entrusted to assistant editor? That's classified

indicators.note: something entrusted to a person is put into their keeping, so inside them

parts.note: asst is short for assistant and ed for editor
OR is the abbreviation for operational research

explanation.surface: A research report is handed to an assistant editor and stamped secret.
explanation.walkthrough: 'classified' suggests secret, but here it means sorted into classes.
explanation.definitionFit: Sorted into kinds or grouped, the sense of classified, is assorted.

clue.text: Dull man associates with respectable married woman

parts.note: matt or mat means dull, not glossy
Ron is a man's name

explanation.surface: A dull man keeps company with a respectable wife.
explanation.definitionFit: A matron is a staid, dignified woman who is married.
